```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 790
library(shiny)

### renderPlot replacement: Safari 27 (WebKit) cannot hold the call stack of
### shiny::renderPlot in webR ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"), so draw with
### renderImage instead, which nests about 45 fewer R calls
renderPlot <- function(expr, width = "auto", height = "auto", res = 72, ...,
                       env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE) {
    func <- shiny::exprToFunction(expr, env, quoted)
    shiny::renderImage({
        info <- shiny::getCurrentOutputInfo()
        w  <- if (is.numeric(width))  width  else info$width()
        h  <- if (is.numeric(height)) height else info$height()
        shiny::req(w > 0, h > 0)
        pr <- shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()$clientData$pixelratio
        if (is.null(pr)) pr <- 1
        f   <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
        dev <- shiny:::startPNG(f, w * pr, h * pr, res = res * pr)
        on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(dev), add = TRUE)
        grDevices::dev.control(displaylist = "enable")
        v <- withVisible(func())
        if (v$visible) print(v$value)
        list(src = f, contentType = "image/png", width = w, height = h,
             coordmap = shiny:::getCoordmap(v$value, w * pr, h * pr, res * pr))
    }, deleteFile = TRUE)
}
library(latex2exp)

d <- 5

log_f <- function(th, d) {
    a <- dnorm(th, -d, log = TRUE); b <- dnorm(th, d, log = TRUE)
    m <- pmax(a, b)
    m + log(exp(a - m) + exp(b - m)) - log(2)
}

log_Ew2 <- function(d, sg) {
    A <- 2 - 1 / sg^2
    if (A <= 0) return(Inf)
    lterm <- function(a, b) {
        m <- (a + b) / 2
        B <- 2 * m + d / sg^2
        C <- 2 * m^2 - d^2 / sg^2
        dnorm(a, b, sqrt(2), log = TRUE) + log(sg) + 0.5 * log(2) +
            0.5 * log(2 * pi / A) - 0.5 * (C - B^2 / A)
    }
    lv <- c(lterm(-d, -d), log(2) + lterm(-d, d), lterm(d, d))
    m  <- max(lv)
    m + log(sum(exp(lv - m))) - log(4)
}

ui <- fluidPage(
    wellPanel(
        fluidRow(
            column(4, sliderInput("sg", HTML("proposal sd &sigma;"), min = 0.25, max = 8,
                                  value = 1, step = 0.05)),
            column(4, sliderInput("S", "sample size  S", min = 100, max = 20000,
                                  value = 2000, step = 100)),
            column(2, numericInput("seed", "seed", value = 11, min = 1, step = 1)),
            column(2, br(), actionButton("new", "New sample")))
    ),
    fluidRow(
        column(9, plotOutput("panels", height = "600px")),
        column(3, h5("Estimates"), htmlOutput("readout"))
    )
)

server <- function(input, output) {

    sim <- reactive({
        S  <- as.integer(input$S); sg <- input$sg
        set.seed(input$seed + 1000 * input$new)

        th   <- rnorm(S, -d, sg)
        logw <- log_f(th, d) - dnorm(th, -d, sg, log = TRUE)
        mx   <- max(logw); v <- exp(logw - mx)
        wn   <- v / sum(v)

        list(th = th, wn = wn, S = S, sg = sg,
             Chat = mean(v) * exp(mx),
             se   = sd(v) / sqrt(S) * exp(mx),
             ess  = 1 / sum(wn^2),
             Ehat = sum(wn * th),
             lsum = mx + log(sum(v)),
             ess_x = 100 * exp(-log_Ew2(d, sg)))
    })

    output$panels <- renderPlot({
        s  <- sim(); th <- s$th; sg <- s$sg
        xr <- range(c(th, -d - 4, d + 4))
        xs <- seq(xr[1], xr[2], length.out = 1000)
        fx <- exp(log_f(xs, d)); gx <- dnorm(xs, -d, sg)
        lwc <- log_f(xs, d) - dnorm(xs, -d, sg, log = TRUE) - s$lsum

        layout(matrix(1:2, 2), heights = c(3, 2))

        par(mar = c(0.4, 5, 3, 1))
        plot(xs, fx, type = "n", ylim = c(0, max(fx, gx) * 1.1), xlim = xr, xaxt = "n",
             xlab = "", ylab = "density",
             main = "bimodal target and a proposal centred on one mode")
        lines(xs, fx, lwd = 4, col = "red")
        lines(xs, gx, lwd = 3, col = "grey60")
        rug(th, col = adjustcolor("grey45", 0.35))
        legend("top", bty = "n", cex = 1.05, text.col = "navy",
               lwd = c(4, 3), col = c("red", "grey60"),
               legend = TeX(c(
                   r"(target $f$)",
                   sprintf(r"(proposal $g$, sd $= %.2f$)", sg))))

        par(mar = c(4.5, 5, 0.4, 1))
        wn <- s$wn
        wl <- c(min(wn) / 5, max(wn) * 5)
        plot(th, wn, type = "n", log = "y", ylim = wl, xlim = xr,
             xlab = expression(theta), ylab = "normalized weight (log scale)")
        lines(xs, exp(pmin(lwc, 700)), lwd = 2, col = "grey25")
        segments(th, wl[1], th, wn, col = adjustcolor("grey45", 0.5))
        abline(h = 1 / s$S, lty = 2, col = "grey55", lwd = 2)
        legend("bottomright", bty = "n", cex = 1.05, text.col = "navy",
               lty = c(2, 1), lwd = c(2, 2), col = c("grey55", "grey25"),
               legend = TeX(c(r"($1/S$)", r"(normalized weight function)")))
    })

    output$readout <- renderUI({
        s <- sim()
        HTML(sprintf(
            "<b>C<sub>f</sub>/C<sub>g</sub></b><br>true 1, est. %.4f<br>
             <b>95%% CI</b> (%.4f, %.4f)<br>
             <b>E<sub>f</sub>(theta)</b><br>true 0, est. %.3f<br>
             <b>observed ESS</b> %.1f%%<br>
             <b>exact ESS</b> %.3g%%<br>
             <b>Var<sub>f</sub>(w)</b> %s",
            s$Chat, s$Chat - 1.96 * s$se, s$Chat + 1.96 * s$se, s$Ehat,
            100 * s$ess / s$S, s$ess_x,
            if (s$sg <= 1 / sqrt(2)) "infinite" else "finite"))
    })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

## About the app

Illustrates how importance sampling can fail without warning when the proposal is too narrow to cover the target. The proposal's standard deviation $\sigma$ is under slider control and both panels are redrawn for each setting. For $\sigma \le 1/\sqrt{2}$ the weight variance is infinite; near $\sigma = 1$ the failure is silent, with the observed effective sample size close to $S$ while the estimate of $C_f/C_g$ sits at one half; past $\sigma \approx 4$ the proposal reaches the second mode, the observed effective sample size falls, and the estimate moves onto the truth.

**The target $f$ and the proposal $g$.** The target is a normalized, equally weighted mixture of two unit-variance normals, with the modes at $\pm d$ and $d=5$,
$$f(\theta)=\tfrac12\,N(\theta\mid -d,\,1)+\tfrac12\,N(\theta\mid d,\,1),$$
and the proposal is a single normal centred on one of the modes, with the standard deviation $\sigma$ set by the slider,
$$g(\theta)=N(\theta\mid -d,\,\sigma^2).$$
Draw $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_S\sim g$ and form the importance weights $w_s=f(\theta_s)/g(\theta_s)$. Because both densities are normalized, $C_f/C_g=1$, and
$$\widehat{C_f/C_g}=\frac1S\sum_{s=1}^S w_s,\qquad \widehat{E_f(\theta)}=\frac{\sum_s w_s\theta_s}{\sum_s w_s},$$
with true values $1$ and $0$. The 95% interval for $C_f/C_g$ is $\hat C\pm1.96\,s_w/\sqrt S$, where $s_w$ is the sample standard deviation of the weights. The quality of the draws is summarized by the effective sample size $S_{\text{eff}}=1/\sum_s\tilde w_s^2$ with $\tilde w_s=w_s/\sum_j w_j$, reported as a percentage of $S$ ("observed"), and by its exact value $S/E_g(w^2)$. The second moment $E_g(w^2)=\int f^2/g$ is finite only when $\sigma>1/\sqrt2$, so for smaller $\sigma$ the weight variance is infinite. The sample size $S$, the seed and a new sample are set in the control panel at the top; the estimates are listed to the right of the plots. The top plot shows $f$ and $g$ on the density scale, and the bottom plot the normalized weights of the draws (log scale), with the dashed line at $1/S$ marking perfectly balanced weights.

The app above varies $\sigma$ with everything else held fixed. Three regimes appear.
Below $\sigma=1/\sqrt{2}$ the variance is infinite and the exact effective
fraction is reported as zero. Between there and roughly $\sigma=3$ the failure is
silent in the sense above: observed $S_{\text{eff}}$ near $S$, estimate near
$\tfrac12$. Past $\sigma\approx4$ the proposal is over-dispersed enough to place
draws near $+d$; the observed $S_{\text{eff}}$ then *drops*, which looks like
deterioration and is in fact the diagnostic finally working, and the estimate
moves onto the truth. The cure for a missed mode is a proposal that is too
diffuse rather than too well matched.
